section: Centre-State administrative relations - Articles 256-263, all-India services, directions to states
subsections: All India Services - Article 312, removal, creation of new services, AIS vs Central Services

accepted.s: Under Article 312 of the Constitution, Parliament may create a new All India Service when the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution supported by:
o: A majority of the members present and voting
Two-thirds of the total membership
A simple majority of the total membership
Two-thirds of the members present and voting
accepted.x: Article 312 requires a Rajya Sabha resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting before Parliament can create a new All India Service.
accepted.tq: Check the exact constitutional majority instead of confusing present-and-voting with total membership.
accepted.sec: All India Services - Article 312, removal, creation of new services, AIS vs Central Services

accepted.s: Which one of the following services is specifically mentioned in Article 312 as capable of being created as an All India Service?
o: Indian Foreign Service
Central Administrative Service
Central Armed Police Service
All India Judicial Service
accepted.x: Article 312 expressly includes the possibility of creating an All India Judicial Service.
accepted.tq: Identify the constitutionally named service rather than an existing Central Service.
accepted.sec: All India Services - Article 312, removal, creation of new services, AIS vs Central Services

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the existing All India Services:
1. The Indian Forest Service was created in 1966.
2. The Indian Foreign Service is an All India Service.
3. The Indian Administrative Service and Indian Police Service are All India Services.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: The Indian Forest Service was created in 1966, and IAS and IPS are All India Services. The Indian Foreign Service is a Central Service, not an All India Service.
accepted.tq: Separate the AIS list from the nearby example of a Central Service.
accepted.sec: All India Services - Article 312, removal, creation of new services, AIS vs Central Services

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes All India Services from Central Services?
o: All India Services are common to the Union and States, whereas Central Services relate to Union subjects only.
Central Services necessarily serve in State cadres, whereas All India Services serve only in Union ministries.
All India Services are confined to Union subjects, whereas Central Services are common to the Union and States.
Both categories are recruited only by State Public Service Commissions.
accepted.x: All India Services are common to the Union and the States, while Central Services are associated with Union subjects only.
accepted.tq: Use the comparison table by splitting the two categories on their field of service.
accepted.sec: All India Services - Article 312, removal, creation of new services, AIS vs Central Services

accepted.s: The Indian Forest Service became an All India Service in:
accepted.x: The Indian Forest Service was created in 1966.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the service-creation year from the years associated with IAS origin and UPSC establishment.
accepted.sec: All India Services - Article 312, removal, creation of new services, AIS vs Central Services

accepted.s:
With reference to All India Services, consider the following statements:
1. Officers are recruited by the Union Public Service Commission on an all-India basis.
2. They serve in State cadres.
3. The Centre recruits and trains them, while they serve under the States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the recruitment, training, cadre allocation and service arrangement of All India Service officers.
accepted.tq: When all statements describe complementary stages of one institutional arrangement, test the complete combination.
accepted.sec: All India Services - Article 312, removal, creation of new services, AIS vs Central Services

accepted.s: The Indian Civil Service was restructured as the Indian Administrative Service in:
accepted.x: The Indian Civil Service was restructured as the Indian Administrative Service in 1947.
accepted.tq: Match the institutional transition with its exact year rather than the year of UPSC replacement or IFoS creation.
accepted.sec: All India Services - Article 312, removal, creation of new services, AIS vs Central Services

accepted.s: Who is associated with describing All India Services as the “Steel Frame” of India?
o: The Chairman of the Finance Commission
Sardar Patel
The Chairman of the Federal Public Service Commission
The Governor-General
accepted.x: Sardar Patel championed the All India Services and referred to them as the “Steel Frame” of India.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive expression with the person associated with it.
accepted.sec: All India Services - Article 312, removal, creation of new services, AIS vs Central Services

accepted.s: The Union Public Service Commission replaced the Federal Public Service Commission in:
accepted.x: The Union Public Service Commission replaced the Federal Public Service Commission in 1950.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional chronology to distinguish the replacement year from the years of cadre-rule and delegation changes.
accepted.sec: All India Services - Article 312, removal, creation of new services, AIS vs Central Services

accepted.s: Which of the following proposals has been made for expanding the scope of All India Services?
o: Restriction of All India Services to Union subjects
Replacement of UPSC recruitment by local recruitment
Abolition of the Indian Administrative Service
Creation of new All India Services for health and education
accepted.x: A proposal has been made to create new All India Services for health and education.
accepted.tq: Identify the constructive expansion proposal rather than an absolute or abolition-based distractor.
accepted.sec: All India Services - Article 312, removal, creation of new services, AIS vs Central Services

accepted.s: Why are All India Services sometimes criticised from the federal perspective?
o: Their officers are governed by Central rules and States lack full control over them.
They are confined entirely to local government administration.
They are recruited exclusively by State Public Service Commissions.
They have no connection with the Union Government.
accepted.x: The federal criticism is that Central rules govern the officers and States do not exercise full control over them, thereby restricting State autonomy.
accepted.tq: Apply the federal-autonomy principle to identify the institutional source of friction.
accepted.sec: All India Services - Article 312, removal, creation of new services, AIS vs Central Services

accepted.s: The proposed amendments to the All India Services (Cadre) Rules, 1954 were associated with which issue?
o: Compulsory retirement of all AIS officers by State Governments
Central deputation without the consent of the State or the officer
Replacement of UPSC recruitment by direct State recruitment
Abolition of State cadres for All India Services
accepted.x: The proposed amendments would enable the Centre to order central deputation without the consent of the State Government or the officer, with the Centre's order becoming final after a prescribed time.
accepted.tq: Focus on the authority and consent issue in the cadre-rule proposal.
accepted.sec: All India Services - Article 312, removal, creation of new services, AIS vs Central Services

accepted.s: Which Article requires that the executive power of every State be exercised so as to ensure compliance with the laws made by Parliament?
o: Article 256
Article 257
Article 365
Article 258
accepted.x: Article 256 requires State executive power to ensure compliance with laws made by Parliament and permits the Union to issue directions for that purpose.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the two adjacent Articles dealing with Union directions to States.
accepted.sec: Centre's directions to states - Articles 256 and 257; non-compliance → Article 365

accepted.s:
Under Article 257, the Union may issue directions to a State regarding:
1. Means of communication of national or military importance.
2. Protection of railways within the State.
3. All matters relating to public order in the State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Article 257 covers communications of national or military importance and protection of railways. Public order is not included in the listed Article 257 direction powers.
accepted.tq: Find the one State List subject improperly added to the specific Article 257 powers.
accepted.sec: Centre's directions to states - Articles 256 and 257; non-compliance → Article 365

accepted.s: A State Government persistently fails to comply with directions issued by the Union under the constitutional scheme. Which provision enables the President to hold that the State government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution?
o: Article 365
Article 258
Article 356
Article 339
accepted.x: Article 365 permits the President to hold that a State government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution when the State fails to comply with Union directions. This can open the way to action under Article 356.
accepted.tq: Trace the consequence chain: non-compliance with Union directions first engages Article 365, which may lead to Article 356.
accepted.sec: Centre's directions to states - Articles 256 and 257; non-compliance → Article 365

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the Article with the subject of Union direction?
o: Article 339 — instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage
Article 257 — communications of national or military importance
Article 365 — delegation of Union functions to State officers by consent
Article 350A — welfare schemes for Scheduled Tribes
accepted.x: Article 257 concerns directions relating to communications of national or military importance. Article 339 concerns Scheduled Tribe welfare, Article 350A concerns mother-tongue instruction, and Article 365 concerns failure to comply with Union directions.
accepted.tq: Use the Article–subject pairing and eliminate swapped constitutional provisions.
accepted.sec: Centre's directions to states - Articles 256 and 257; non-compliance → Article 365

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the effect of different emergencies on Union directions to States?
o: A Financial Emergency automatically transfers all State executive power to the Union.
During a National Emergency, the Union loses the power to issue directions; during a Financial Emergency, directions concern only defence.
During a National Emergency, directions may extend to any matter; during a Financial Emergency, directions concern canons of financial propriety.
Both emergencies permit directions only regarding protection of railways.
accepted.x: A National Emergency permits Union directions on any matter, whereas a Financial Emergency is associated with directions concerning canons of financial propriety.
accepted.tq: Compare the scope of Union directions under the two emergencies without treating them as identical.
accepted.sec: Centre's directions to states - Articles 256 and 257; non-compliance → Article 365

accepted.s: Under Article 258(1), functions of the Union may be entrusted to a State Government or its officers by:
o: The President, with the consent of the State Government
The Governor, without the consent of the Union Government
The Supreme Court, with the consent of the President
Parliament, only with the consent of the State Legislature
accepted.x: Article 258(1) empowers the President to entrust Union functions to a State Government or its officers with the consent of the State Government.
accepted.tq: Ask who entrusts the function and whether consent is required; these are the main Article 258(1) traps.
accepted.sec: Delegation of functions - Articles 258 and 258A

accepted.s: A law made by Parliament entrusts a Union function to a State or its officers without obtaining the State Government's consent. This arrangement is authorised by:
o: Article 258(2)
Article 258A
Article 258(1)
Article 257
accepted.x: Article 258(2) permits Parliament, by law, to confer functions relating to Union matters on a State or its officers without the State's consent.
accepted.tq: Distinguish delegation by presidential entrustment from delegation made directly by parliamentary law.
accepted.sec: Delegation of functions - Articles 258 and 258A

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct position under Article 258A?
o: The Governor entrusts State functions to the Union with the consent of the Government of India.
Parliament entrusts Union functions to States with State consent.
The Union Cabinet entrusts State functions to the Governor without consent.
The President entrusts State functions to the Union without consent.
accepted.x: Article 258A enables the Governor to entrust functions of the State to the Union or its officers with the consent of the Government of India.
accepted.tq: Reverse the direction of delegation carefully: Article 258A deals with State-to-Union entrustment.
accepted.sec: Delegation of functions - Articles 258 and 258A

accepted.s: Article 258A was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
o: The First Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951
The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978
The Seventh Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976
accepted.x: Article 258A was inserted by the Seventh Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956.
accepted.tq: Link the Article with the specific amendment year while avoiding the nearby 42nd Amendment association.
accepted.sec: Delegation of functions - Articles 258 and 258A

accepted.s: The principal constitutional purpose of delegation under Articles 258 and 258A is to:
o: Transfer all State executive powers to Parliament
Make every State function subject to prior judicial approval
Avoid rigidity and deadlock in administration
Abolish the distinction between Union and State subjects
accepted.x: Delegation under these Articles provides flexibility in administration and helps avoid rigidity and deadlock between the Union and the States.
accepted.tq: Identify the functional purpose of a constitutional mechanism rather than its formal procedure.
accepted.sec: Delegation of functions - Articles 258 and 258A

accepted.s:
Arrange the following provisions in chronological order of their constitutional amendment or institutional origin:
A. Creation of the Indian Forest Service
B. Insertion of Article 258A
C. Replacement of the Federal Public Service Commission by UPSC
D. Restructuring of ICS as IAS
o: D, C, B, A
C, D, B, A
D, B, C, A
C, B, D, A
accepted.x: The correct sequence is IAS restructuring in 1947, UPSC replacing the Federal PSC in 1950, insertion of Article 258A in 1956, and creation of IFoS in 1966.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last dates, then place the 1950 and 1956 events between them.
accepted.sec: All India Services - Article 312, removal, creation of new services, AIS vs Central Services

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding deployment of armed or central forces in a State is correct?
o: Such deployment is prohibited because public order and police are Union List subjects.
The Union can deploy them only after obtaining the State Government's consent.
Only the State Legislature can authorise their deployment.
The Union may deploy them with or without the State's consent in discharge of its Article 355 duty.
accepted.x: The Union may deploy armed or central forces with or without State consent in discharge of its duty under Article 355.
accepted.tq: Test the consent issue directly and distinguish constitutional duty from State List allocation.
accepted.sec: Armed forces and central forces deployment in states - consent issue

accepted.s: The constitutional basis associated with Union deployment of armed or central forces in States is:
o: Entry 2A of the Union List, inserted through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment
Entry 97 of the Concurrent List, inserted through the First Amendment
Entry 1 of the State List, inserted through the Seventh Amendment
Entry 2 of the State List, inserted through the 44th Amendment
accepted.x: Entry 2A of the Union List, associated with the 42nd Constitutional Amendment, provides the relevant Union List basis for deployment.
accepted.tq: Match the entry, list and amendment together instead of relying on the general subject of policing.
accepted.sec: Armed forces and central forces deployment in states - consent issue

accepted.s: Why do States object to the Union's deployment of armed or central forces without their consent?
o: All emergency powers are exclusively State powers.
Public order and police are State List subjects.
Railways and military affairs are State List subjects.
Defence and communications are State List subjects.
accepted.x: States object because public order and police fall in Entries 1 and 2 of the State List, making deployment a sensitive issue concerning State authority.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific State List subjects rather than broader security-related subjects.
accepted.sec: Armed forces and central forces deployment in states - consent issue

accepted.s: The Administrative Reforms Commission of 1966 supported deployment of forces by the Centre:
o: Only after a resolution of the State Legislature
On the request of the State or otherwise
Only when the Governor requests it
Only during a Financial Emergency
accepted.x: The 1966 Administrative Reforms Commission supported deployment “on their request or otherwise,” meaning that a State request was not treated as indispensable.
accepted.tq: Test the precise wording of the recommendation, especially the alternative expressed by “or otherwise.”
accepted.sec: Armed forces and central forces deployment in states - consent issue

accepted.s: Which recent development concerning Central Armed Police Forces is correctly stated?
o: A 2025 Supreme Court order abolished all CAPF cadres and transferred them to State police forces.
The Supreme Court directed that CAPF officers must be deputed only to State cadres.
The Central Armed Forces (General Administration) Bill had already abolished the CAPF system in 2025.
A 2025 Supreme Court order granted CAPF officers Organised Group A status and sought to reduce IPS deputation.
accepted.x: The 2025 Supreme Court order referred to granting CAPF officers Organised Group A status and reducing IPS deputation. A Central Armed Forces (General Administration) Bill was expected in response.
accepted.tq: Separate the actual institutional reform from exaggerated abolition or transfer claims.
accepted.sec: Armed forces and central forces deployment in states - consent issue

accepted.s: Approximately how many CAPF officers were referred to in connection with the expected Central Armed Forces (General Administration) Bill?
accepted.x: The figure referred to was approximately 13,000 CAPF officers.
accepted.tq: Read the place value carefully when distinguishing a reported approximate figure from scaled-up distractors.
accepted.sec: Armed forces and central forces deployment in states - consent issue
